transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Tyrell (Redwood SE), Anya Sullivan (Redwood CSM), Ravi Patel (FalconStream Lead ML Eng), Maria Gomez (FalconStream Platform Eng), Tom Hsu (FalconStream CTO)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough):
- Quick go-around, review of TTFT numbers from last sprint, discuss microburst spikes and sequence-length shifts after quantization change, decide next benchmark window.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: ok hey everyone thanks for joining on a friday, um we'll keep this tight, Marcus is gonna drive the results section and then we'll go into the microburst plan.
[00:23] Marcus: yeah hi all, so quick context, we ran three variants last week: hosted baseline, dedicated with burst tier, and a hedged path with earlier KV cache warm. The TTFT numbers, uh, median improved ~12% on the dedicated path but tails still show spikes around the microburst windows.
[00:47] Ravi: when you say spikes, are we talking 95th to 99th or like 99.9? that's really what moves our SLA.
[01:05] Marcus: mostly 95th to 99.5. the 99.9 is rare but when the streaming buffer collapses we saw 2x increase. it's tied to sequences longer than 1024 tokens, and also a kernel fallback we triggered during certain batch sizes.
[01:30] Maria: sorry, kernel fallback? can you unpack that, i thought you said kernel auto-select should prefer the fused matmul path?
[01:41] Marcus: sure, so the runtime picks a fast matmul kernel for seqlen patterns it recognizes, but when we had long sequences and microburst concurrency, it fell back to a slower generic kernel. there might be a mis-heuristic in the kernel selector.
[02:05] Tom: is that the thing you call the "stitch" path? i've heard redwood mention it in docs.
[02:12] Lena: yeah some teams call it stitch or slowpath, sometimes first token fastpath (ttft) vs slowpath on subsequent tokens. apologies the transcriber sometimes mashes names, but the idea is we prefer an early fast kernel for short responses.
[02:29] Ravi: ok got it. what's the work to change the selector? do we need a code release or is it a config?
[02:38] Marcus: depends. in our canary we adjusted a threshold in the policy layer (cheap) and saw improvement, but a robust fix would be a small runtime patch to better weight concurrency and seqlen variance. that patch needs a deploy on Dedicated nodes.
[02:59] Maria: for Dedicated, what's the isolate/tenant story? we want deterministic tail behavior, and noisy neighbors are a concern.
[03:08] Lena: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools plus optional burst capacity. noisy neighbor mitigation is via scheduling and reservation; we also provide hedging/circuit policies to route to fallback models in other pools when a node's overloaded.
[03:27] Ravi: are you capturing KV cache warm rates? we saw cold-starts that align w/ our traffic patterns.
[03:33] Marcus: yes, KV cache warm is logged, but our autoscaler warm-up policy can be tuned. for this test we'll enable prefix caching more aggressively to reduce first-key misses. sometimes the transcriber reads KV as K-V cash, so ignore that in the notes :)
[03:53] Tom: (laughs) yeah saw that. also security question: we need KMS/HSM options and audit logs for compliance — SOC2 coverage?
[04:03] Lena: we have SOC2 reports, KMS integrations for Private deployment and Dedicated via our control plane, and audit logs in the Console. i'll attach the pack after this call.
[04:13] Anya: we'll also note SSO/SAML and RBAC options in the pack, and the options for on-prem if FalconStream needs air-gap.
[04:23] Maria: good. coming back to latency, you mentioned quantization noise earlier — what did you observe?
[04:30] Marcus: small model quant decisions you made (the 4-bit path) reduced memory and improved throughput but the sequence-length distribution shifted slightly; we saw more token regen in some prompts which inflate TTFT because of additional decoding passes.
[04:49] Ravi: are we able to simulate our prompt set? we can provide sanitized examples.
[04:55] Lena: yes please, that helps a lot. Marcus, if they share a representative 100K event sample we'll run it under the 48h microburst window.
[05:06] Marcus: yep that's the plan. also want to try streaming buffer adjustments — shorten handshake, earlier flush on partial responses — it trimmed the first token path for some internal tests.
[05:23] Tom: how invasive are those streaming changes? any risk to token-level cost?
[05:29] Marcus: there's a slight throughput vs cost tradeoff. aggressive streaming reduces TTFT but increases per-token overhead in small fragments. we can tune by route: production-critical routes get aggressive streaming, low-value routes get batched.
[05:46] Maria: route level config is good for us, we have mixed traffic. do you support per-model routing rules?
[05:52] Lena: yes per-route and per-model; Console shows per-token cost and latency.
[05:58] Ravi: any thoughts on hedging or multi-model fallback? sometimes switching to a slightly smaller model improves tail.
[06:06] Marcus: we can do that automatically via policy: if the primary model exceeds a latency threshold, route to a verified smaller variant. quality gates prevent large degradation.
[06:16] Tom: what's the expected impact on tail if you enable that? numbers?
[06:21] Marcus: from previous pilots: hedging dropped 99th by ~25% in mixed traffic but increased median cost by ~8%. it's a net improvement for tight SLAs.
[06:33] Ravi: ok fair. for the microburst test plan, what metrics should we watch?
[06:39] Marcus: TTFT median/95/99/99.9, streaming handshake latency, kernel fallback counts, KV cache hit rate, and CPU/GPU occupancy. we'll also measure token regen rate and aborted streams.
[06:54] Maria: about kernel selection, can we get a trace showing when selector flips? that would help debug heuristics.
[07:00] Marcus: yes we'll export a selector trace per request id, though it's sampling to avoid volume. we'll include a sample in the runbook.
[07:12] (brief cross-talk)
[07:20] Ravi: i want to ask about the Dedicated burst tier pricing you mentioned last time, is that included or add-on?
[07:28] Lena: it's an add-on to Dedicated, billed monthly with a commit and overage. i'll send the updated pricing sheet today.
[07:35] Tom: and if we do Private on-prem, is the runtime identical? we care about parity and rollouts.
[07:42] Marcus: runtime is feature-parity, some integrations differ (on-prem uses customer KMS and local networking). deployment steps are similar but packaging differs.
[07:53] Maria: how long does it take to deploy the runtime in our VPC?
[07:57] Lena: standard Private deploy is 4-6 weeks including network and security review, faster if you're comfortable with self-hosted infra assumptions.
[08:08] Ravi: can we stage: do dedicated pilot first then Private if needed?
[08:12] Lena: that's a common path, yes. Dedicated pilot gives you fast feedback.
[08:18] Marcus: i want to call out one anomaly: on the hedged tests we observed an edge-case where the kernel path selection misclassified sequences when batching hit 32 concurrency and seqlen around 800-1100. it's an ML-informed heuristic and we'll patch it.
[08:37] Maria: ok will that require an outage?
[08:40] Marcus: no outage, need to ship a runtime patch and restart workers in the pool during a maintenance window.
[08:48] Tom: what's the risk to inference correctness?
[08:51] Marcus: none on correctness, only performance. the fallback is slower but returns identical outputs.
[08:58] Ravi: good. about the microburst window — what load shape will you run?
[09:03] Marcus: we'll run step bursts simulating realistic session spikes: baseline QPS, then 30s bursts at 4-6x for a 10-20 minute window repeated across the day to simulate concurrency spikes. also random long sequences injected at 2% to emulate big prompts.
[09:21] Maria: can you replicate our region topology? we run multi-region failover so cross-region latency matters.
[09:27] Marcus: we can simulate cross-region latency in the bench harness; please share desired RTT numbers.
[09:33] Ravi: ~60ms inter-region typical, occasionally 120ms.
[09:37] Marcus: noted.
[09:40] (brief pause)
[09:48] Anya: quick ops note — we'll enable more verbose tracing for the benchmark window and rotate logs to your S3 bucket if you want.
[09:54] Ravi: yes please, we'll take the logs. how do we share the S3 bucket creds securely?
[09:59] Lena: we can use presigned upload endpoints and temporary STS tokens, or if you prefer we can pull logs from your exposed endpoint. we'll work with your security team.
[10:12] Tom: one more Q on evals — can we lock a prompt set for quality regression checks? we don't want hedging to hurt quality.
[10:18] Marcus: absolutely, Redwood Optimize can tie quality monitors to prompt sets and alert on regressions. during hedging we ensure eval thresholds before failover.
[10:28] Maria: timeline — you said you'll prepare the microburst plan and send pricing and security docs by monday?
[10:34] Lena: yes, Lena to send pricing and Anya will attach security docs. Marcus posts test plan by monday.
[10:41] Ravi: and we'll aim to deliver the sanitized traffic sample by wed 22nd.
[10:46] Marcus: ok then schedule the benchmark window for sept 24-26 as proposed.
[10:52] Tom: please include our SRE on the runbook.
[10:55] Anya: will do.
[11:00] (wrap)
